founding: In the spring of the first year, {abbot} and {brothers} brothers came to the ruin at {place}. They cleared the rubble from the old chapel, sang Vespers under a broken roof, and dedicated the house to {patron}.

In the spring of the first year, {abbot} led {brothers} brothers up the road to {place}, where a chapel of the old world still stood without its windows. There they founded the house of {patron}, with three sacks of seed and one goat.

In the spring of the first year, {abbot} and {brothers} brothers came over the hill to {place}, the last house on the western edge of Ireland, where the road runs out at the sea. They found the chapel roofless and the wind coming through it, and dedicated the house to {patron}.
death_age: {When}, {monk} died in his sleep at {age_words} years of age, and was buried beside the chapel.
{When}, {monk}, {age_words} years old, asked for the sacraments after Compline and was dead before Lauds. The brothers said he had been ready for some time.
{When}, {monk} went to God in the fullness of his years. He was {age_words}, and had outlived the world he was born in.
death_illness: {When}, {monk} did not recover from his sickness. He was buried in the brothers' field, facing east.
{When}, the fever took {monk}. The healers did what they could, and the brothers kept vigil until the end.
{When}, {monk} died of a sickness of the chest after many weeks in the infirmary.
election_after_death: After the burial of {old}, the brothers met in chapter and chose Brother {new_name} as their abbot.
When the bell had been tolled for {old}, the brothers elected Brother {new_name} to lead the house. He wept, and did not refuse.
election_after_departure: With {old} gone from the house, the brothers met in chapter and chose Brother {new_name} as their abbot.
Since {old} was no longer among them, the brothers elected Brother {new_name} in his place.
hunger: {When}, the granary ran empty and hunger came to the house. The brothers ate nettle soup and kept the Office all the same.
{When}, there was no bread. The brothers fasted though it was no fast day, and some grew weak.
cold: {When}, the woodpile was gone and the cold came into the dormitory. The old brothers suffered most.
{When}, there was nothing left to burn, and the brothers slept in the chapel together for the warmth.
harvest_good: The harvest of the {year_ordinal} year was good. The granary was full by Michaelmas, and the abbot ordered a Te Deum.
In the {year_ordinal} year the fields gave generously, and the house went into winter without fear.
harvest_fair: The harvest of the {year_ordinal} year was neither good nor bad, and the brothers gave thanks for it.
In the {year_ordinal} year the harvest was enough, if the winter was not long.
harvest_poor: The harvest of the {year_ordinal} year was poor, and the brothers looked at the granary and said nothing.
In the {year_ordinal} year the fields failed them. The abbot ordered the rations cut before the first frost.
winter_begins: Winter came early to {place} that year, and the stream froze before Advent.
The first snow fell on the chapel roof, and the brothers moved the scriptorium desks closer to the fire.
built_granary: {When}, the granary was finished at the north wall, and its first bin was filled with grain from the stores.
{When}, the brothers raised a granary of stone with walls thick enough to keep out the damp and the mice.
built_woodshed: {When}, a woodshed was roofed against the wall, and the stacked logs were covered before the rain came.
{When}, the brothers built a woodshed open to the south, so the wood would dry before the cold.
built_infirmary: {When}, the old guest room was turned into an infirmary, with straw pallets, a boiling pot and shelves for the jars.
{When}, the brothers set up an infirmary in the east cloister, where the light is best for sewing wounds.
built_scriptorium: {When}, a scriptorium was made in the south cloister, with desks by the window and a shelf for the inks.
{When}, the scribes moved their desks into a room of their own, where the damp was least.
generation_turns: {When}, a new cohort of brothers took their places in the choir, and the house entered its {gen_ordinal} generation.
novice_joins: {When}, a young man came to the gate and asked to be received. He was clothed as a novice and called {monk}.
{When}, {monk} knocked at the gate in the rain, and the brothers took him in as a novice.
saint_acclaimed: {When}, the brothers and the people of the glen began to call {monk} a saint. Pilgrims came to his grave with candles.
colony_departure: {When}, {party} left the house to found a daughter house at {node}, with a letter from the abbot and a sack of seed.
priory_founded: {When}, {party} raised the first daughter house of {patron} at {node}, and the people there came to see them settled.
priory_lost: {When}, the people of {node} closed their doors to the daughter house, and it was given up.
priory_tithe: {When}, the daughter house at {node} sent {food} measures of grain to the mother house at harvest.
rule_changed: {When}, the chapter took up {option} as the house's rule of {axis}.
road_departure: {When}, {party} set out along the road for {node}.
{When}, {party} left the gate with a sack of bread and a letter for {node}.
road_arrival_generic: {When}, {party} reached {node}, and found the people there wary of the house.
{When}, {party} came to {node} and were given a place by the fire, though little was said.
return_generic: {monk} came home from the road with little to tell.
{monk} returned to the house, footsore, and went straight to the chapel.
house_fell: Here the annals of the house of {patron} at {place} end. No brother remained to keep them.
And the house of {patron} fell silent. The wind came in through the chapel windows as it had before the brothers came.
feast_kept: On the feast of {feast} the brothers kept the whole office and sang High Mass with the doors open to the road.
On the feast of {feast} the bell was rung at every hour, and the house ate better than it had any right to.
On the feast of {feast} the brothers walked the boundary wall in procession, singing, as the old rule asks.
skill_rose: {monk} has grown to the level of {level} in {skill}, and the house has begun to rely on him for it.
After many weeks at it, {monk} reached the level of {level} in {skill}. The older brothers said nothing, which was their praise.
training_done: {monk} finished his weeks of learning {skill} and went back to his own work, a little surer of his hands.
The weeks of learning {skill} were done for {monk}, and he returned to the house's work with more to give it.
training_begun: {monk} was set to learn {skill} from {teacher}, and his usual work passed to another pair of hands.
training_alone: {monk} was set to learn {skill} alone, from the old books, which is slow work. He knew it and did not complain.
